patient_record: Initial consultation. Diagnosis: mesial-tilted impaction; buccal impaction; pulpitis. Treatment: extraction recommended; pulpitis management; crown defect restoration.
chief_complaint: The patient reports recurrent food impaction around tooth 48 for several years, causing intermittent discomfort.
present_illness: Over the past few years, the patient has experienced repeated food trapping at the site of tooth 48, prompting today’s evaluation.
past_medical_record: The patient denies any recent travel to high-risk areas, contact with COVID-19 cases, or systemic illnesses.
examination: Tooth 48 shows mesial impaction with carious lesions on contacting surfaces. Tooth 47 has a distal carious defect with cold sensitivity but no percussion pain, gingival inflammation, or mobility. Tooth 18 is buccally displaced with occlusal caries. Tooth 16 has a fractured enamel–dentin area with exposed dentin, negative cold and percussion tests, healthy gingiva, and no mobility.
radiographs_examination: CBCT reveals that the lesion on tooth 47 extends into the pulp chamber; no periapical pathology is noted for teeth 16, 18, or 48.
diagnosis:
* Tooth 48: Mesial impaction
* Tooth 18: Buccal impaction
* Tooth 47: Pulpitis
treatment_plan:
* Extract teeth 18 and 48
* Perform root canal therapy on tooth 47
* Restore tooth 16 with a crown or inlay
treatment_recommendations:
* Extraction of teeth 18 and 48 to resolve impaction issues
* Root canal therapy followed by post-core and crown on tooth 47
* Full-coverage restoration of tooth 16
management: For tooth 47, the patient was informed of the diagnosis, plan, costs, and prognosis and provided consent. Local anesthesia and caries removal were performed, revealing pulp exposure; a pulpotomy was placed with a devitalizing agent. A provisional restoration was placed and the patient scheduled for definitive root canal therapy in one week. For tooth 48, flap elevation, crown-root sectioning, atraumatic removal, socket irrigation, gelatin sponge placement, and single-suture closure were carried out. For tooth 18, surgical extraction with curettage and hemostasis using a gelatin sponge were performed.
medical_instructions: Avoid biting hard foods. If pulpal symptoms occur, return for root canal therapy. Follow standard post-extraction care and take prescribed antibiotics as needed. Suture removal in one week.

patient_record: Follow-up consultation. Diagnosis: Dental caries; supernumerary tooth. Treatment: Resin restoration.
chief_complaint: Referred from orthodontics for tooth extraction.
present_illness: Referred from orthodontics, seeking extraction.
examination: Tooth 17 has buccal-occlusal caries, negative percussion, normal gingiva, and normal cold test. Tooth 24 is intact with normal gingiva and no other notable findings.
diagnosis: Tooth 17: Dental caries; Tooth 24: Supernumerary tooth.
treatment_plan: Tooth 17: Resin restoration.
management: For tooth 17, caries removal was performed using a high-speed handpiece and chemical gel, followed by cavity preparation. The area was cleaned, dried, etched, rinsed, and dried again. A bonding agent was applied, thinned, and cured. Resin was incrementally filled and cured, then shaped, adjusted, and polished. For tooth 24, local disinfection with povidone-iodine and infiltration anesthesia with prilocaine were administered. After anesthesia took effect, the gingiva was separated, the tooth was loosened, and extracted with forceps. Routine curettage of the extraction site and pressure hemostasis were performed.
medical_instructions: Return if discomfort occurs, bite on gauze for 40 minutes, avoid brushing or rinsing for 24 hours, eat after 2 hours, avoid hot foods and hard biting.

Gingival margins are red, soft, and thickened, with blunt papillae and a gingival sulcus depth of 1 mm. BI: 1, DI: 3, no attachment loss.
radiographs_examination: No radiographs taken.
treatment_plan: Supragingival scaling with ultrasonic and air polishing.
management: Oral hygiene instruction, brushing technique guidance, and flossing advice. Explained condition, treatment plan, costs, and prognosis to the patient, who consented. treatment_plan_cn: 超声龈上洁治术；喷砂洁治术。

medical_instructions_cn: 一周内禁进酸性食物,避冷热刺激。禁咖啡、茶、可乐等含色素饮品，禁止吸烟。保持口腔卫生，漱口水含漱。定期复查，不适随诊。

management: For teeth [0][DE][ED][0], the patient was informed about the condition, treatment plan, costs, and prognosis and consented to treatment. patient_record: Follow-up consultation. Diagnosis: Pulpitis (K04.005).
chief_complaint: Continuation of treatment one week after root canal therapy.
present_illness: The patient reports no issues one week after root canal therapy and has returned for further treatment.
examination: Tooth 47: Temporarily sealed. Tooth 37: Proximal caries reaching deep dentin, positive response to cold and heat tests.
management: Tooth 47: Rubber dam was applied, temporary seal removed, medicament was retrieved, and the pulp chamber was opened. Three canals were located, and pulp extirpation was attempted with minor bleeding. Hand files were used to negotiate canals to size 15#, with a working length of 17mm. Canal preparation was assisted by Glyde and performed with rotary nickel-titanium instruments. Canals were irrigated, dried, and filled with SP and gutta-percha, base was placed, and GIC was used for temporary sealing. Tooth 37: The condition, treatment plan, costs, and prognosis were explained to the patient, who consented to treatment. Local infiltration anesthesia was administered with compound articaine. Carious tissue was removed, revealing pulp exposure with significant bleeding. The pulp exposure was enlarged and sealed with arsenic-free devitalizing agent, and Cervitron was used for temporary sealing.
medical_instructions: Return for follow-up if discomfort arises.

chief_complaint: The patient returns for continued treatment of the upper right anterior teeth two weeks after initial therapy.
present_illness: The patient reports no discomfort following treatment of the upper right anterior teeth two weeks ago and returns for further treatment.
examination: Tooth 12 shows no percussion sensitivity or gingival inflammation and is temporarily sealed. Tooth 34 is rotated and positioned outside the arch with a proximal deep carious lesion reaching the dentin layer. Tooth 33 has a proximal deep carious lesion extending to deep dentin with cold-induced pain.
diagnosis:
* Teeth 12, 33: Pulpitis (K04.005)
* Tooth 34: Deep caries in permanent teeth (K02.800x008)
management: For tooth 12, the temporary seal was removed, post space prepared, and a resin fiber post was bonded. Abutment teeth were prepared and refined. Silicone impressions and bite records were taken, and a temporary crown was placed. For tooth 33, local infiltration anesthesia with 4% Articaine was administered, pulp chamber accessed, pulp extirpated, rubber dam placed, canal orifices located, and pulp removed. The coronal third of the canal was prepared with GG drills, a #15 K-file was used to determine the canal length, confirmed by radiograph at 20mm. The canal was prepared using a large taper technique to F2, irrigated alternately with sodium hypochlorite and saline, dried, and temporarily sealed with calcium hydroxide paste. For tooth 34, local disinfection with povidone-iodine, local infiltration anesthesia with Bilanma, gingival separation, tooth luxation, and extraction with forceps were performed. The extraction site was curetted and pressure applied for hemostasis.
medical_instructions: Return if any discomfort occurs. Bite on cotton roll for 40 minutes, avoid brushing and rinsing for 24 hours, and refrain from eating for 2 hours. Avoid hot foods.

past_medical_record_cn: 高血压(-)、心脏病(-)、糖尿病(-)病史，肝炎(-)及结核(-)等传染病史接触史。过敏史(-),余系统回顾未见明显异常。否认发病前28天内有境外、中高风险地区的旅居或途径史，或有病例报告社区的旅居史，否认发病前28天内与新型冠状病毒感染者(核酸检测阳性者)有接触史，否认发病前28天内管接触过来自境外，或来自有病例报告社区的发热或呼吸道症状的患者否认聚集性发病(28天内在小范围如家庭、办公室、校班级等场所，出现2例及以上发热和/或呼吸道症状的病例)。
examination_cn: 口腔卫生状况一般，牙面可见大量色色素附着。牙石++,尤以下颌前牙舌侧及双侧后牙颊侧为重。牙龈缘充血色红，质地松软，边缘厚钝，龈乳头圆钝，龈沟深度1 mm,BI:1,Dl:1,无附着丧失。
treatment_plan_cn: 超声龈上洁治术，喷砂洁治术。
management_cn: 口腔卫生宣教，指导刷牙方式及牙线使用。已向患者交代清楚患牙情况及费用，患者知情同意后，全口龈上洁治，喷砂，抛光，上药。
medical_instructions_cn: 一周内禁进酸性食物，避冷热刺激。禁咖啡、茶、可乐等含色素饮品，禁止吸烟。保持口腔卫生，漱口水含漱。定期复查，不适随诊。

patient_record: Initial consultation. Diagnosis: Tooth structure defect, apical periodontitis; dental crowding.
chief_complaint: The patient reports a decayed upper right posterior tooth for one month.
present_illness: Several years ago, the patient underwent root canal treatment and resin filling at an external clinic. One month ago, part of the resin fell out, leading to a tooth structure defect and affecting eating.
past_medical_record: The patient is generally healthy with no systemic diseases or drug allergies.
examination: Tooth 16: Large mesial occlusal defect with caries extending subgingivally, fiber post in the root canal, negative percussion and gingival tests, no mobility. The patient reports gingival inflammation one week ago. Teeth 26 and 27: Not erupted, thick gingiva.
radiographs_examination: Tooth 16: CBCT shows well-filled root canal with low-density area at the apex. Teeth 26 and 27: CBCT shows tooth 26 above tooth 27, with fully developed roots. General dental crowding.
diagnosis: Tooth 16: Tooth structure defect, apical periodontitis; dental crowding.
treatment_plan: Tooth 16: Recommend resin filling and monitor prognosis. If inflammation recurs, consider extraction and implant restoration in adulthood. Teeth 26 and 27: Recommend referral to orthodontics for traction and alignment.
management: For tooth 16, the patient and guardian were informed of the condition, treatment plan, costs, and prognosis, and consented to treatment. The patient was advised that resin filling would be attempted, but due to the large defect, the filling might dislodge. Local infiltration anesthesia with 4% Articaine was administered, gingival tissue was trimmed to expose the tooth structure, caries were removed, a matrix band was placed, etching was performed, and the area was isolated and dried. Bonding agent was applied and cured, Voco resin was layered and cured, occlusion was adjusted, and the restoration was polished.
medical_instructions: Avoid chewing on the affected side for 2 hours. Follow-up if discomfort occurs. Avoid hard foods.
anomalies_en: Periapical Periodontitis,Tooth Structure Loss,Dental Crowding,Dental Caries

chief_complaint: The patient returns for continued treatment of the upper right anterior tooth, two weeks post initial treatment.

examination: Tooth 12 shows no percussion pain or gingival inflammation. Temporary sealing is present. Tooth 34 is rotated and buccally positioned with a large carious lesion on the proximal surface extending to dentin. Tooth 33 has a deep carious lesion on the proximal surface extending to deep dentin with cold-induced pain.
diagnosis: Pulpitis of teeth 12 and 33 (K04.005); deep caries of tooth 34 (K02.800x008).
management: For tooth 12, temporary sealing was removed, post space preparation was done, and a resin fiber post was bonded. The abutment was prepared and refined. Silicone impressions and bite registrations were taken for temporary crown fabrication. For tooth 33, local infiltration anesthesia with 4% articaine was administered. Pulp chamber access was gained, pulp extirpated, rubber dam applied, and canal orifices located. The coronal third was prepared with GG drills, and the canal length was determined to be 20mm using an apex locator. Canal preparation was completed with rotary files to F2, followed by alternating irrigation with sodium hypochlorite and saline, drying, and temporary sealing with calcium hydroxide paste. For tooth 34, local disinfection with povidone-iodine and infiltration anesthesia with prilocaine were administered. After anesthesia onset, the gingiva was separated, the tooth luxated, and extracted with forceps. The socket was curetted and hemostasis achieved by pressure.
medical_instructions: Return for follow-up if any discomfort occurs. Bite on cotton roll for 40 minutes, avoid brushing or rinsing for 24 hours, and refrain from eating for 2 hours. Consume food that is not too hot.

examination: Tooth 48 is partially erupted with no gingival inflammation and adequate mouth opening.
radiographs_examination: X-ray shows mesial impaction of tooth 48.
treatment_plan: Extraction of tooth 48.
management: For tooth 48, local disinfection with povidone-iodine was performed. Inferior alveolar nerve block anesthesia with lidocaine hydrochloride and local infiltration with articaine were administered. After anesthesia took effect, gingival separation was performed, and the crown was sectioned to relieve mesial obstruction. The tooth was extracted in sections using an elevator and forceps. Routine curettage of the extraction socket and suturing for hemostasis were completed.
medical_instructions: Follow-up if discomfort occurs. Bite on a cotton roll for 40 minutes. Avoid brushing or rinsing for 24 hours. Start eating after 2 hours, avoiding hot foods. Self-provided anti-inflammatory medication is recommended.

Tension-free suturing was performed, and radiographs confirmed positioning. Impressions were taken for transitional dentures, and occlusion was adjusted and polished.

patient_record: Initial consultation. Diagnosis: Dental caries (K02.901). Treatment: Composite resin restoration.
chief_complaint: The patient reports tooth discoloration for several weeks.
present_illness: The patient has noticed darkening of teeth over several weeks and seeks dental care.
past_medical_record: Generally healthy with no significant medical history.
examination: Teeth 11, 12, 21, 22, and 37 show carious lesions. Tooth 11 has distal caries, tooth 21 has mesial and distal caries, tooth 22 has mesial caries, and tooth 37 has occlusal and buccal caries extending to the deep dentin layer. The gingiva appears normal.
radiographs_examination: Teeth 11, 12, 21, 22, and 37 show low-density shadows reaching the dentin layer.
treatment_plan: Composite resin restorations for teeth 11, 12, 21, 22, and 37.
management: The patient was informed of the diagnosis, treatment plan, costs, and prognosis and consented to treatment. Caries removal, cavity preparation, application of caries gel, softening of carious tissue, and removal with excavation tools were performed. The cavity was cleaned, dried, etched, rinsed, and dried again. A bonding agent was applied, thinned, and light-cured. A matrix was placed, and 3M-P60 resin was incrementally filled, light-cured, shaped, occlusally adjusted, and polished.
medical_instructions: Return for follow-up if discomfort occurs. Avoid biting hard foods. If pulpal symptoms develop, root canal therapy may be necessary.

The canal was temporarily sealed with paste and glass ionomer. A post-operative radiograph confirmed proper filling. For tooth 35, the patient was informed of the condition, treatment plan, costs, and prognosis, and consented to treatment. Caries removal was incomplete, exposing the pulp. For tooth 21, under local anesthesia, endodontic access was made, the canal was cleaned, length measured at 19mm, irrigated, and temporarily sealed with calcium hydroxide.

examination: Tooth 47 shows no obvious occlusal caries, distal cervical cold sensitivity, negative percussion, positive bite test, no gingival inflammation or mobility. Tooth 48 shows mesial inclination with the crown pressing against tooth 47's cervical region, with large bifurcation angles of the roots, no other abnormalities.
treatment_plan: Tooth 47: Root canal therapy with crown restoration recommended; patient opts for root canal therapy first. Tooth 48: Extraction recommended.
management: For tooth 47, the patient was informed about the condition, treatment plan, costs, and prognosis, and chose root canal therapy first. Local infiltration anesthesia with 4% Articaine was administered, occlusal access was made, distal caries removed, coronal pulp extirpated, arsenic-free devitalizing agent and eugenol cotton pellet placed, and temporarily sealed. Root canal preparation scheduled for one week. For tooth 48, inferior alveolar nerve block and local infiltration anesthesia with 4% Articaine were administered, gingiva separated, crown sectioned into mesial and distal parts, atraumatic luxation and extraction performed, curettage, repositioning, saline irrigation, gelatin sponge and Palyoc placed, single suture, and pressure hemostasis. Suture removal in one week.
medical_instructions: Avoid biting hard foods. If pulpal symptoms occur, return for root canal therapy. Follow post-extraction care instructions, take oral antibiotics if needed, and return if discomfort occurs. Suture removal in one week.

Treatment: Option 1: Root canal treatment for teeth 15 and 34, crown removal and implant restoration for teeth 14, 35, and 36. Option 2: Root canal treatment for tooth 15, crown removal and implant restoration for tooth 14, crown removal for teeth 34, 35, and 36, extraction of tooth 34, and implant-supported bridge restoration. The patient chose option 1.
chief_complaint: The patient reports pain in both sides of the mouth for several days.
present_illness: The patient describes continuous pain in both sides of the mouth for several days, with gingival swelling, seeking treatment.
past_medical_record: No significant medical history.
examination: Teeth 14, 35, and 36 are missing, with self-curing resin material and wire fixation to adjacent teeth, soft tissue swelling. Tooth 15 shows distal surface discoloration, a buccal sinus tract, soft tissue proliferation, mobility grade II, and percussion pain (++). Tooth 34 has buccal soft tissue swelling, a wedge-shaped groove at the cervical area with smooth edges, black surface, soft probing, pulp exposure, mobility grade II, negative cold test, and percussion pain (++).
radiographs_examination: Teeth 15 and 34 show low-density images in the apical region, with buccal alveolar bone resorption to the apex for tooth 34.
diagnosis: Teeth 14, 35, and 36: Dental arch defect (K08.100x002). (Poor restoration). Teeth 15 and 34: Chronic apical periodontitis (K04.500).
treatment_plan: Option 1: Root canal treatment for teeth 15 and 34, crown removal and implant restoration for teeth 14, 35, and 36. Option 2: Root canal treatment for tooth 15, crown removal and implant restoration for tooth 14, crown removal for teeth 34, 35, and 36, extraction of tooth 34, and implant-supported bridge restoration. The patient chose option 1.
management: For teeth 14, 35, and 36, the patient was informed about the condition, treatment plan, costs, and prognosis, and consented to treatment. Local infiltration anesthesia with compound articaine was administered, and crowns were removed. For teeth 15 and 34, the patient was informed about the condition, treatment plan, costs, and prognosis, and consented to treatment. Pulp chamber access was performed, pulp roof was removed, canal orifices were explored, and pulp was extirpated. GG drills were used to prepare the coronal third of the canal, and an 08# C-file was used to explore canal length. An apex locator measured the palatal root length at 18mm, buccal root length at 18mm, and tooth 34 length at 18mm. Canals were prepared using large taper rotary technique, and nickel-titanium files were used to enlarge to F2. Canals were ultrasonically irrigated with 1% sodium hypochlorite and distilled water, alternately rinsed with sodium hypochlorite and saline, dried, and temporarily sealed with calcium hydroxide paste.
medical_instructions: Return if discomfort occurs. Avoid biting hard objects. Follow-up in one week.

management: The patient was informed about the diagnosis, treatment plan, costs, and prognosis, and consented to the treatment. Local infiltration anesthesia with compound articaine was administered, followed by pulp chamber opening and pulp removal. The coronal third of the canal was prepared with GG drills, and the canal length was determined to be 18mm using an apex locator. The canal was prepared using a large taper rotary technique with NiTi files up to F3. The canal was ultrasonically irrigated with 1% sodium hypochlorite and distilled water, and a master cone was fitted. The canal was dried with paper points and obturated with sealer and gutta-percha. A post-operative radiograph confirmed adequate filling. Composite resin was used for coronal restoration, followed by shaping, occlusal adjustment, and polishing.

examination: Teeth 17, 27, and 47 exhibit occlusal caries, with negative percussion and gingival tests, and normal cold testing. Tooth 22 shows palatal caries with similar test results.
treatment_plan: Resin restoration for teeth 17, 22, 27, and 47.
management: For teeth 17, 22, 27, and 47, caries removal gel was applied to the cavities, followed by thorough caries removal and cavity preparation. examination: Teeth 26 and 46 show poor oral hygiene with significant plaque and pigmentation, caries extending to mid-dentin, negative cold test, negative percussion, and normal gingival color. radiographs_examination: Teeth 26 and 46 show caries extending to the dentin layer.
diagnosis: Teeth 26 and 46: Moderate caries in permanent teeth (K02.800x007). Tooth 36: Deep caries in permanent teeth (K02.800x008).
treatment_plan: Full-mouth plaque management, caries restoration for teeth 26, 36, and 46.
management: For teeth 26 and 46, oral hygiene instruction was provided, including brushing, flossing, and use of interdental brushes. Caries gel was applied to soften carious tissue, which was then removed with excavation tools. Cavities were prepared, etched with 35% acid, bonded, and filled with 3M P60 resin, followed by occlusal adjustment and polishing. For tooth 36, caries gel was applied, carious tissue removed, pulp exposure occurred, base placed with BP, and temporarily sealed with Fuji IX.
medical_instructions: Avoid sticky and hard foods for 24 hours. Return for follow-up if discomfort occurs.
remarks: Patient cooperation was low, preventing vital pulp therapy. If pulpitis symptoms develop, root canal treatment will be necessary, as informed to the guardian. Pulp protection was performed on tooth 36, to be observed for one week.

patient_record: Follow-up consultation. Diagnosis: Secondary caries (K02.800x001); Pulpitis (K04.005).
chief_complaint: Impression taken for upper anterior teeth one week ago.
present_illness: The patient had an impression taken for the upper anterior teeth one week ago with no discomfort and is returning for follow-up.
examination: Tooth 12: negative percussion, healthy gingiva, temporary crown present. Tooth 17: negative percussion, healthy gingiva, temporarily sealed.
management: Tooth 17: Rubber dam was placed, temporary seal removed, canal orifice explored, and pulp extirpated. The coronal third was prepared with GG drills, canal length determined with a #15 K-file and apex locator, all canals measured 17mm. Canals were prepared using a large taper rotary technique to F3. Sodium hypochlorite and saline were used alternately for irrigation, canals were dried, and calcium hydroxide paste was used for temporary sealing. Tooth 12: Temporary crown and sealant were removed, abutment and restoration cleaned, restoration margins checked for fit, and proximal contacts verified. Occlusion was adjusted, polished, and permanently cemented.
medical_instructions: Return for follow-up if discomfort occurs.

management: For tooth 36, the temporary crown and sealing material were removed. The abutment and restoration were cleaned, and the restoration was tried in for proper fit and contact. past_medical_record: History of hypertension, controlled with medication. Blood pressure: 135/76 mmHg.
examination: Generalized moderate to severe gingival recession, bleeding on probing, tooth displacement, and periodontal pockets detected. Poor oral hygiene with a debris index (DI) of 1 and calculus index (CI) of 1, indicating supragingival calculus covering less than one-third of the tooth surface. Attachment loss and subgingival calculus detected, with a bleeding index of 4 (bleeding fills and overflows the gingival sulcus upon probing). Gingiva is swollen and dark red with loss of stippling. Teeth 15, 24, 25, 26, 31, 32, 35, 37, 41, 42 show moderate to severe gingival recession, mobility grade III, negative probing, and percussion (±). Teeth 36, 47 are residual roots with caries and mobility grade II, negative probing, and percussion (±). Tooth 21 is missing with a mesiodistal gap of 5mm and an occlusogingival distance of 5mm, with alveolar ridge resorption.
radiographs_examination: Generalized moderate to severe alveolar bone resorption.
diagnosis: Periodontitis (K05.301). Residual roots on teeth 36, 47. Dental arch defect (K08.100x002) on tooth 21.
treatment_plan: Systematic periodontal treatment.
management: For teeth 11, 12, 13, 14, 16, 17, 22, 23, 31, 32, 33, 34, 43, 44, 45, 46, the patient was informed of the condition, treatment plan, costs, and prognosis, and consented to treatment. Local infiltration anesthesia with compound articaine was administered, followed by subgingival scaling, root planing, laser treatment, and polishing. Hydrogen peroxide and saline irrigation were performed, and periodontal dressing was applied. Oral hygiene instruction (OHI) was provided, including brushing, flossing, and interdental brush use. For tooth 15, povidone-iodine disinfection and local infiltration anesthesia with compound articaine were performed. After anesthesia, gingival separation and extraction with forceps were carried out, followed by routine curettage of the extraction socket and pressure hemostasis.

patient_record: Follow-up consultation. Diagnosis: Dental crowding (K07.302) with reduction in tooth number; potential impaction (K01.100); dental caries (K02.901). Treatment: Extraction and resin restoration.
chief_complaint: Referred from orthodontics for tooth extraction.
present_illness: Referred from orthodontics seeking tooth extraction.
examination: Tooth 14 is intact with healthy gingiva. Tooth 48 is unerupted with healthy gingiva. Teeth 17, 27, 37, and 47 have occlusal caries, negative percussion, healthy gingiva, and normal cold test response.
radiographs_examination: Tooth 48 shows low-position impaction.
diagnosis:
* Tooth 14: Dental crowding (K07.302) with reduction in tooth number.
* Tooth 48: Potential impaction (K01.100).
* Teeth 17, 27, 37, 47: Dental caries (K02.901).
treatment_plan:
* Extraction of teeth 14 and 48.
* Resin restoration for teeth 17, 27, 37, and 47.
management: For tooth 48, local disinfection with povidone-iodine was performed, followed by inferior alveolar nerve block anesthesia with lidocaine and local infiltration with articaine. After anesthesia onset, gingival separation and crown sectioning were done, and the tooth was extracted with forceps. The extraction site was curetted and sutured for hemostasis. For tooth 14, local disinfection and infiltration anesthesia were applied, followed by gingival separation and extraction with forceps. The site was curetted and compressed for hemostasis. For teeth 17, 27, 37, and 47, caries removal gel was applied, caries were excavated, cavities were prepared, cleaned, and dried. Acid etching, bonding agent application, and layered resin filling were performed, followed by occlusal adjustment and polishing.
medical_instructions: Follow up if discomfort occurs. Bite on gauze for 40 minutes. Avoid brushing or rinsing for 24 hours. Eat after 2 hours, avoiding hot foods.

management_cn: 48号牙齿，局部聚维酮碘消毒，盐酸利多卡因下齿槽神经阻滞麻醉，复方阿替卡因适量局部浸润麻醉。待麻药发挥效果后分离牙龈，手机磨切分割牙冠部分，挺松，拔牙钳取出。常规搔刮拔牙创，缝合止血。14号牙齿，局部聚维酮碘消毒，复方阿替卡因适量局部浸润麻醉。待麻药发挥效果后分离牙龈，拔牙钳取出。常规搔刮拔牙创，压迫止血。17,27,37,47号牙齿，将祛腐凝胶放入龋洞，去腐工具去龋净，备洞。清洁吹干，酸蚀剂酸蚀，冲洗吹干。涂布粘接剂，吹薄，光照。树脂分层填入，分层光固化，修形、恢复窝沟形态，调颌、抛光。
medical_instructions_cn: 嘱不适随诊，咬棉卷40 min，24h不刷牙漱口，2h后可饮食，建议饮食不要太热。

chief_complaint: The patient returns for continued treatment one week after root canal therapy.
present_illness: The patient reports no issues one week after root canal therapy and presents for further treatment.
examination: Tooth 22 is temporarily sealed. Teeth 17, 46, and 47 have occlusal caries extending to the middle dentin layer, with normal cold and heat tests. Teeth 14, 24, 34, and 44 are fully erupted and require extraction as per orthodontic consultation.
diagnosis: Moderate caries of teeth 17, 46, and 47 (K02.800x007); malocclusion of teeth 14, 24, 34, and 44.
treatment_plan: Fillings for teeth 17, 46, and 47; extractions for teeth 14, 24, 34, and 44.
management: For tooth 22, isolation was applied, temporary seal was removed, medicament was retrieved, and the pulp chamber was accessed. One canal was located, and pulp extirpation was incomplete with slight bleeding. Hand files were used to negotiate the canal to size 15, with a working length of 22.5mm. Canal preparation was done using NiTi rotary instruments with Glyde assistance. The canal was irrigated, dried, and the master cone was trial-fitted to working length. The canal was obturated with warm gutta-percha, a base was placed, and the access was filled with composite. For teeth 17, 46, and 47, carious dentin was removed to the deep dentin layer without pulp exposure. Shade matching was done, gingival retraction was applied, and the proximal restoration system was used. Pulp protection and base placement were followed by composite restoration, occlusal adjustment, and polishing. For teeth 14 and 44, the patient was informed about the condition, treatment plan, costs, and risks, and consented to extractions. Local infiltration anesthesia with compound articaine was administered, gingiva was separated, teeth were luxated and extracted, sockets were curetted, irrigated with saline, and gelatin sponges were placed for hemostasis.
medical_instructions: Return for follow-up if discomfort occurs. Bite on cotton roll for 40 minutes, avoid brushing or rinsing for 24 hours, and avoid eating for 2 hours. Recommend avoiding very hot foods.

patient_record: Follow-up consultation. Diagnosis: Partial edentulism (K08.100x002).
chief_complaint: The patient reports missing lower left posterior teeth for several months.
present_illness: The patient has experienced difficulty eating due to missing lower left posterior teeth for several months and seeks treatment.
past_medical_record: The patient is in good health with no significant medical history. Denies systemic conditions.
examination: Teeth 34, 35, and 36 are missing with a mesiodistal gap of 25.5 mm and an occlusogingival distance of 5 mm. The alveolar ridge is resorbed with no supraeruption of opposing teeth. Overall oral hygiene is fair with presence of calculus and staining. No significant occlusal or joint abnormalities noted.
radiographs_examination: Radiographs show alveolar bone width of 5.1 mm and height of 11 mm in the area of missing teeth 34, 35, and 36.
management: Informed consent for implant restoration was obtained. Preoperative antibiotics were administered. Local anesthesia with articaine was used. A horizontal incision was made at the crest of the ridge, and a full-thickness flap was reflected. Osteotomy sites were prepared, and Dentium implants were placed: 3.4x10 mm for site 34 and 4.3x8 mm for site 36. Cover screws were placed, bone graft material was applied, and the flap was sutured with tension-free closure. Postoperative radiographs confirmed implant positioning.
medical_instructions: Strict adherence to post-implant care instructions is required. Oral antibiotics should be taken as prescribed. Follow-up for suture removal in two weeks.

patient_record: Follow-up consultation. Diagnosis: Secondary caries; deep caries. Treatment: Composite resin restoration.
chief_complaint: The patient reports no significant discomfort and continues treatment today.
examination: Teeth 43, 44, 45, and 46 exhibit dark carious lesions at the cervical area extending to deep dentin, with cold sensitivity in teeth 43 and 46.
radiographs_examination: Teeth 44 and 45 show adequate root canal fillings. Teeth 43 and 46 have deep caries.
diagnosis: Teeth 44 and 45: Secondary caries. Teeth 43 and 46: Deep caries.
management: For teeth 43 and 46, caries removal to deep dentin, pulp protection, base placement, and composite resin restoration were performed. Occlusal adjustment and polishing were done. The patient was informed that root canal therapy might be needed if postoperative pain occurs. For teeth 44 and 45, abutment preparation and refinement were completed, and silicone impressions and bite registrations were taken for temporary crown restoration.
medical_instructions: Return for follow-up if discomfort occurs.

patient_record: Follow-up consultation. Diagnosis: Moderate caries in permanent teeth (K02.800x007). Treatment: Resin restoration.
chief_complaint: The patient reports darkening of posterior teeth on both sides for several days.
present_illness: Darkening of posterior teeth on both sides for several days, seeking examination.
past_medical_record: Healthy with no significant medical history. Denies drug and food allergies.
examination: Poor oral hygiene with plaque accumulation at the cervical margins. Occlusal caries present, negative to probing, cold, and percussion tests. Gingiva appears normal.
treatment_plan: Resin restoration for tooth 46.
management: Applied caries gel to soften carious tissue, removed decay, prepared cavity, etched with 35% phosphoric acid, applied bonding agent, and restored with VOCO resin to recreate occlusal anatomy. Adjusted occlusion and polished. Provided oral hygiene instruction, including brushing and flossing techniques. Applied fluoride varnish after plaque disclosure and polishing.
medical_instructions: Educate on oral hygiene, including brushing, flossing, and interdental brush use.
remarks: Consider preventive or restorative treatment for teeth 17, 16, 26, 27, 37, and 47 at the next visit.
